cohort: 82 pregnancies in 56 subjects with bleeding disorders who delivered at a single center from 2010 to 2021
finding: The study found no statistically significant difference in the rate of postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) between vaginal and cesarean deliveries in pregnant individuals with bleeding disorders.
mod_finding: While not statistically significant, the study found an odds ratio of 0.7 (95% CI, 0.1-3.4) for primary PPH and 2.6 (95% CI, 0.4-16.4) for secondary PPH when comparing vaginal and cesarean deliveries.
